142.canonical: Before treating work as done, require an adversarial review by a dedicated subagent in a fresh context on only the diff/query and the acceptance criteria; fix blocking correctness findings and re-review rather than letting the producing agent approve its own output.

154.canonical: Do not rely on Zero Data Retention for Agent Skills — Skill definitions and execution data fall under Anthropic's standard retention policy — so keep ZDR-required sensitive data out of Skills.

156.canonical: Test each skill against every model it will run on, and write instructions detailed enough for the least-capable target model without over-explaining for stronger ones.

157.canonical: Author valid frontmatter: a name of at most 64 characters (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens; no XML tags or reserved words) and a non-empty description of at most 1024 characters with no XML tags.

160.canonical: Always use forward-slash file paths in skill instructions and references so skills work across platforms, including Unix.

161.canonical: Give a single sensible default with an escape hatch, mentioning alternatives only briefly, rather than presenting many equal options.

163.canonical: Bundle reusable deterministic scripts for recurring, mechanically-checkable operations and have the agent run them by default instead of regenerating the code, since bundled scripts are more reliable, cheaper, faster, and more consistent.

164.canonical: When inputs can be rendered as images, have the model inspect them visually to reason about spatial layout, form structure, and other visual properties.

170.canonical: Retrieve a Skill-generated file through the Files API: extract its file ID from the code-execution tool result (checking both Python and bash result blocks) and download the content.
